links.outcome: LLM responses to counterfactual, dangerous or implausible medical evidence supplied as context
links.effect: Models overwhelmingly accepted counterfactual evidence at face value, even when dangerous or implausible, rather than rejecting it. Exact rates not given in the abstract.
links.quote: Our evaluation across multiple frontier LLMs on MedCounterFact reveals that in the presence of counterfactual evidence, existing models overwhelmingly accept such "evidence" at face value even when it is dangerous or implausible, and provide confident and uncaveated answers.

links.outcome: Confidence and caveats in LLM answers given counterfactual medical evidence
links.effect: Models gave confident, uncaveated answers when the evidence was counterfactual, dangerous or implausible. Exact rates not given in the abstract.
links.quote: Our evaluation across multiple frontier LLMs on MedCounterFact reveals that in the presence of counterfactual evidence, existing models overwhelmingly accept such "evidence" at face value even when it is dangerous or implausible, and provide confident and uncaveated answers.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluation of LLM safety and faithfulness when presented with counterfactual or adversarial medical contexts.
